description: Original behavioral evaluations. Grade meaning and requested operation, not exact wording.

cases.prompt: NORMALIZE this descriptive policy text: Operators should save a copy before they update the package. Operators must record the installed version.
invariants: Saving a copy remains a recommendation, not a requirement.
Recording the installed version remains mandatory.
The recommendation to save a copy still applies before the update.
failure_examples: Changes should to must or an unqualified command.
Changes must to should, may, or can.
Removes or reverses the temporal condition.

cases.prompt: NORMALIZE this incident description: The log was deleted during the update. The available evidence does not identify who or what deleted it.
invariants: The deletion remains a reported event during the update.
The actor remains unknown.
The update is not presented as the cause merely because it coincided with the deletion.
failure_examples: Invents an operator, administrator, software process, or other actor.
Changes during to because of.
Rejects passive voice despite the explicitly unknown actor.

cases.prompt: NORMALIZE this procedure: Open valve V-2 only if the pressure is less than 4 kPa and the indicator is green.
invariants: Both conditions remain necessary before opening the valve.
The pressure comparison remains strictly less than 4 kPa.
The valve identifier and indicator color remain unchanged.
failure_examples: Changes and to or.
Changes less than to at most or less than or equal to.
Gives an unconditional command followed by the conditions.

cases.prompt: NORMALIZE this procedure. The quoted strings are exact interface labels: Press the “DON'T RESET; HOLD” button after the display shows “Colour check complete”.
invariants: Preserves the exact label DON'T RESET; HOLD, including its apostrophe and semicolon.
Preserves the exact label Colour check complete, including British spelling and capitalization.
The display message must precede pressing the button.
failure_examples: Expands DON'T inside the label.
Removes the semicolon inside the label.
Changes Colour to Color.
Reverses the condition and action.

cases.prompt: VALIDATE only. Do not rewrite the text or provide a corrected version. Review this procedure: Don't open the panel; record the serial number.
invariants: Reports findings without supplying a rewritten or corrected procedure.
Identifies the contraction and the semicolon with applicable rule IDs 4.2 and 8.1.
Does not claim full dictionary compliance was assessed.
failure_examples: Returns a revised procedure, even after a valid report.
Labels all words approved without supporting evidence.
Claims full compliance or certification.

cases.prompt: NORMALIZE this procedure: Before you replace it, disconnect the sensor from the controller.
invariants: Recognizes that it can refer to the sensor or the controller.
Asks which component is to be replaced before choosing a definitive rewrite.
Preserves the required ordering of disconnection before replacement.
failure_examples: Silently chooses the sensor or controller.
Deletes the replacement condition to remove the ambiguity.
Presents an assumed interpretation as the final revision.

cases.prompt:
VALIDATE only this system description. Do not rewrite it. Review paragraph structure and sentence count with specific rule IDs. The following is one paragraph:

The archive stores service records. Each record has a unique identifier. The archive retains records for one year. The reception lights use a separate circuit. A wall switch controls those lights. The switch is beside the door. The lights have no connection to the archive.
invariants: Identifies seven sentences in one paragraph under 6.6.
Identifies the two different topics under 6.5 rather than a section-wide range.
Reports findings without a rewritten paragraph.
Does not claim full dictionary verification.
failure_examples: Uses only 6.1–6.6 for a finding.
Invents a causal link between archive storage and lighting.

cases.prompt:
VALIDATE only the safety instruction below, with specific rule IDs. Do not rewrite it. Context for this fictional manual: the governing convention uses CAUTION for this equipment-damage risk. An abrasive cloth can scratch the optical window. That explanation is absent from the instruction. Instruction text:

The window needs attention. Wipe the window with the specified soft cloth.
invariants: Cites 7.1 for the missing applicable risk identifier.
Cites 7.2 for starting with a description instead of a command or necessary condition.
Cites 7.3 for the missing risk or consequence explanation.
Does not invent injury hazards or change equipment damage into a different severity.
Preserves VALIDATE-only scope and states that full dictionary compliance was not assessed.
failure_examples: Cites only 7.1–7.3.
Provides a rewritten safety instruction.
